syllabusTopics: Introduction: Three domains of life, binomial nomenclature, five kingdom classification system (Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia)
Status of flora in Nepal and world representation
Fungi: General introduction and characteristic features of phycomycetes, ascomycetes, basidiomycetes and deuteromycetes
Structure and reproduction of Mucor and Yeast
Introduction of Mushrooms, poisonous and non-poisonous mushrooms, economic importance of fungi
Lichen: General introduction, characteristic features and economic importance of lichen
Algae: General introduction and characteristic features of green, brown and red algae; structure and reproduction of Spirogyra; economic importance of algae
Bryophyta: General introduction and characteristic features of liverworts, hornworts and moss; morphological structure and reproduction of Marchantia; economic importance of bryophytes
Pteridophyta: General introduction and characteristic features of pteridophytes; morphological structure and reproduction of Dryopteris; economic importance of pteridophytes
Gymnosperm: General introduction and characteristic features of Gymnosperms; morphology and reproduction of Pinus; economic importance of gymnosperm
Angiosperm: Morphology of root, stem, leaves, inflorescences, flowers and fruit
Taxonomic study: Definition, taxonomic hierarchy, classification systems (artificial, natural and phylogenetic) of angiosperms

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Angiosperms are the most diverse and successful plant group, with seeds enclosed in fruits. The flower is the reproductive organ, consisting of sepals, petals, stamens (male), and carpels (female). Monocots and dicots differ in root type, leaf venation, flower structure, and cotyledon number. NEB focuses on four families — Brassicaceae, Fabaceae, Solanaceae, and Liliaceae — and their economic importance.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Flower parts: Sepal (protection) + Petal (attraction) + Stamen (male: anther + filament) + Carpel (female: ovary + style + stigma)
Fruit types: Simple, Aggregate, Multiple
Monocot: fibrous root, parallel venation, 3-parted flower, one cotyledon

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Angiosperms produce BOTH seeds AND fruits; gymnosperms produce seeds only (no fruit).  ·  Monocots have parallel venation, fibrous roots, and 3-parted flowers; dicots have net venation, taproots, and 4-or-5-parted flowers.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects a detailed, labelled diagram of a complete angiosperm flower.  ·  The four NEB families (Brassicaceae, Fabaceae, Solanaceae, Liliaceae) must be tabulated with diagnostic features.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Oryza sativa — rice; monocot; family Poaceae; staple food of Nepal.  ·  Brassica juncea — mustard; dicot; family Brassicaceae; oil and vegetable crop.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The carpel (gynoecium) is the female part of the flower; the stamen is the male part.  ·  Brassicaceae flowers have 4 petals in a cross shape (cruciform); Solanaceae have 5 petals (rotate-symmetric).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Label a complete flower  ·  Tabulate 4 NEB families

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Flower = S-P-S-C (Sepal, Petal, Stamen, Carpel).  ·  Brassicaceae = 4 petals (cross); Fabaceae = pea-shape (zygomorphic); Solanaceae = 5 petals; Liliaceae = 6 tepals.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Differentiate monocot and dicot plants (5 points).  ·  Describe the structure of a complete angiosperm flower with a labelled diagram.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Draw and label a complete angiosperm flower — very common.  ·  Tabulate 4 NEB families (symmetry, petal number, fruit type, example).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Flower structure (4 whorls)  ·  Monocot vs dicot  ·  4 NEB families  ·  Fruit types

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Angiosperms: seeds enclosed in fruit; ~300,000 species.  ·  Flower: sepal + petal + stamen (male) + carpel (female).  ·  Monocots vs dicots: root, venation, flower parts, cotyledon number.  ·  NEB families: Brassicaceae (4 petals), Fabaceae (zygomorphic), Solanaceae (5 petals), Liliaceae (6 tepals).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Angiosperms are the most species-rich plant group: ~300,000 species worldwide.  ·  Rice (Oryza sativa) is the most important food crop in Nepal; it belongs to family Poaceae.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Tabulate the four NEB angiosperm families with their diagnostic features.  ·  Explain the economic importance of each of the four NEB families.  ·  Describe the taxonomic hierarchy of a Nepali plant (e.g., Oryza sativa or Brassica juncea).

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Differentiate monocot from dicot (5 points).  ·  Describe the taxonomic hierarchy of a Nepali plant.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Pisum sativum — pea; dicot; family Fabaceae; nitrogen-fixing legume.  ·  Solanum tuberosum — potato; dicot; family Solanaceae; tuber crop.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: The female reproductive part of an angiosperm flower is: → B  ·  Which family is characterised by a four-petaled, cross-shaped flower? → C

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Angiosperms (flowering plants): seeds enclosed in a fruit; include ~90% of all plant species; the most diverse and successful plant group.  ·  Flower structure: perianth (sepals + petals), androecium (stamens: anther + filament), gynoecium/pistil (carpel: ovary + style + stigma).  ·  Root: taproot (dicots) or fibrous (monocots); functions: absorption, anchorage, storage.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Taxonomic hierarchy  ·  Classification systems  ·  Economic importance

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Dicot: taproot, net venation, 4/5-parted flower, two cotyledons  ·  Taxonomic hierarchy: Division > Class > Order > Family > Genus > Species.  ·  Classification systems: Artificial, Natural, Phylogenetic.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Fabaceae flowers are zygomorphic (bilaterally symmetric); most other angiosperm flowers are actinomorphic (radially symmetric).  ·  An inflorescence is the arrangement of flowers; it is NOT a single flower.  ·  Lilium — tulip/lily; monocot; family Liliaceae; ornamental.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Monocot vs dicot differentiation is a very frequent short-answer.  ·  Economic importance of each family is a common application question.  ·  Taxonomic hierarchy questions: know the ranks and give a plant example.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Memorise the structure of a complete flower (all 4 whorls).  ·  Learn the diagnostic features of the 4 NEB families (petal number, symmetry, fruit type).  ·  Practice writing the taxonomic hierarchy of Oryza sativa and Brassica juncea.
